$schema_comment: Aviation obstruction lighting on tall structures.
At night, correctly marked obstacles are how you read vertical development from the cockpit.
Marking follows FAA AC 70/7460-1 in outline - a flashing beacon at the top, steady red side
lights at intermediate levels roughly every 150 ft below it.
which searches OpenStreetMap inside every area declared in data/region.json. Entries can
also be written by hand, and hand-written ones are the right answer for a structure OSM has
no height for - the sweep skips those rather than guessing at an altitude.
A re-sweep REPLACES this list. Anything hand-added is lost, so record a structure the sim
already lights in `sweep.exclude` in config/build_profile.json instead of deleting it here.
`levels` is generated automatically from height_ft when `auto_levels` is true: one ring of
steady side lights every `level_interval_ft` below the top, per the AC's guidance.
HEIGHTS come from OSM height tags, which are contributed rather than surveyed. Do not use
this package as an obstacle database - it is scenery.
$marking_comment: FAA AC 70/7460-1 allows a structure to be marked with red lights or with medium-intensity
white strobes, and both are in common use.
The white scheme is not just a colour swap. A white system strobes at every level including
the top, uses fewer levels than a red one, and carries three units per level rather than
four - so it gets its own interval and count rather than inheriting the defaults.
Marking is the one field OSM cannot supply: it records that a structure is there, not what
the authority had it painted or lit with. The sweep therefore proposes red for anything new,
and carries an existing choice over when a swept structure lands on top of one.
OUTSIDE THE UNITED STATES these numbers are wrong. ICAO Annex 14 marks from 45 m rather than
200 ft and spaces levels differently. Edit the schemes here - nothing in tools/ hard-codes
